title: Head, Innovation Hubs
description: About us Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. About the role Moniepoint is building innovation hubs at three of Nigeria’s leading universities: Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), and Ahmadu Bello University (ABU). Each hub is a cross-disciplinary platform, open to students from every faculty. The model is cohort-based, industry-connected, and built to produce technical talent ready for the job market, across software engineering, AI, product, data science, robotics, and design. The hubs train students in applied technical skills, connect them to working engineers, product leaders, and founders, and provide a path into industry at Moniepoint, at other technology companies, or through ventures of their own. This is a building role. The hubs are entering their operating phase, and you will own the design of how they run and the teams that run them. What you will own Programme design. You will design the operating model for all three hubs from the ground up: how cohorts are structured, how learning is sequenced, what “job market-ready” means at each level, and how graduates are assessed and certified. This is not adapting someone else’s playbook. It is writing one. University relationships. You will be the primary relationship owner with the Vice-Chancellors, deans, faculty leads, and student bodies at OAU, UNN, and ABU. These are institutional relationships that require both strategic seniority and sustained presence. Cross-faculty engagement. The hubs are not engineering faculty initiatives. They are open to students across every faculty: engineering, sciences, humanities, business, design. You will design the engagement model that brings students from across each university into the hub and keeps them in it through the full cohort. Industry and mentorship pipeline. The hubs derive their value from the connection between classroom and industry. You will build and manage the network of engineers, product leaders, and founders, inside Moniepoint and beyond, who mentor, assess, and hire from the hubs. Facilitators and standard.  You will design the facilitator model, recruit the people who teach and assess, and own the standard those facilitators hold the cohort to. A single standard across all three hubs is non-negotiable; how it's delivered locally is yours to design. Infrastructure and operations. You will own the physical footprint of each hub, whether that means a buildout from scratch or working within an existing campus structure, and manage the timelines, vendor relationships, and hub-level budgets across three sites. You will define the staffing model for each hub and recruit the on-ground team that runs them day to day. Outcomes and accountability. You will set and own the metrics: graduate output, job placement, programme completion, cohort quality, employer satisfaction. Pipeline integration. The hubs are upstream of Moniepoint Academy and other talent programmes. You will design the connective tissue between hub graduates and Moniepoint’s internal pathways, so the strongest talent has a clear next step. Who you are 10+ years of experience overall, with at least 5 in leadership roles owning programmes, teams, and budgets end to end. You have built or led a technical training or workforce development programme at scale, ideally across multiple sites. You have taken something from zero to one - designed the model, hired the team, and held the standard yourself. You have held institutional relationships at senior level across universities, government bodies, and industry partners. You know how to navigate Nigerian university administration, or you have done it elsewhere and can credibly do it here. You have hired and managed technical educators, and you know what separates someone who can teach from someone who can teach to a standard. You understand what good engineering education looks like and what employers in software, AI, product, and data science actually hire for. You don't need to write code, but you need the technical fluency to design a programme that produces hireable engineers, not credentialed graduates. You are rigorous about outcomes and impatient with programmes that look good in announcements but cannot prove what they produce. Experience in edtech, developer education, university-industry partnerships, or workforce development is a strong signal. Building something from scratch and owning it through to measurable outcomes is essential. What success looks like Year one. Operating model live across all three hubs. Cohorts running on a common standard. The facilitator team hired and held to the same expectations regardless of site. First graduate cohort exited, with a clear placement record into Moniepoint and into industry. Year two. The hubs are recognised within Nigeria as the most credible cross-disciplinary technical training environment available to undergraduates. Employers, including Moniepoint, actively hire from the hubs. Cohort demand outstrips supply. Year three. Hubs producing technical talent into Moniepoint at a cost-per-hire that justifies the investment, and into the wider industry at a scale and quality that defines what a corporate-funded university programme can look like in Nigeria. Model documented and ready to expand if leadership chooses. What Moniepoint can offer you The opportunity to shape one of the most consequential talent infrastructure investments in Nigerian technology.  A dynamic, diverse, and collaborative environment where every team member's voice is recognised and valued.  Continuous learning and career growth opportunities.  Competitive salary, individual performance bonuses, and firmwide performance bonus. Company-covered health insurance plans. Pension plans. What to expect in the hiring process A preliminary conversation with one of our recruiters. An interview with the hiring manager, our Head of Corporate Affairs. A case study or written exercise on operating model design for the hubs. An interview with our Group COO. A final conversation with our CEO.

title: Head of Debt Collections
description: About Moniepoint Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions and process over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. JOB PURPOSE The Head, Debt Collection is a strategic leadership position tasked with the architecture and execution of Moniepoint’s debt collection framework. The primary focus of this role is the minimization of Loss Given Default (LGD) within both the business and consumer lending divisions.   The incumbent will oversee, develop, and implement comprehensive and versatile debt collection strategies designed to manage a diverse portfolio of credit products, ranging from digital-first retail lending to large-ticket corporate financing.   Responsibilities include designing the organizational structure of the debt collection unit and recruiting high-caliber talent. Additionally, specialized expertise in debt litigation and asset recovery will be required to navigate complex cases of delinquency.   A data-driven methodology must be utilized to systematically evaluate the efficacy of recovery tactics and the performance of personnel.   Job Responsibilities  Design and implement a segmented debt collection framework — differentiated by product type, ticket size, and delinquency stage — spanning early-stage soft collections through hardcore legal recovery, restructuring, and write-off pathways. Define the org structure, recruit high-caliber talent, and stand up the operational and systems infrastructure (collections management systems, tracking dashboards, agent/dialer tooling) needed to run recovery at scale. Direct legal recovery strategy for the department — whether executed directly or through instruction of external counsel — ensuring all actions comply with applicable financial regulations and debt collection laws. Manage high-level engagements with external stakeholders, including law enforcement agencies, regulatory bodies, and external counsel, to expedite resolution of non-performing loans (NPLs). Design incentive structures and performance frameworks (KPIs, commission or fee structures) for the collections and recovery network to drive both recovery rate and cost-to-collect efficiency. Continuously train and upskill the collections and recovery network in alignment with collections  strategy and industry best practice. Own collections and recovery performance reporting to senior management, including recovery rate, cost of recovery, and portfolio-level LGD trends, and feed recommendations into credit committee decisions on write-offs and restructuring. Collaborate with credit, legal, risk, and finance to align collections and recovery efforts with underwriting standards and portfolio strategy. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in a relevant field. Minimum 7 years of experience in credit/debt recovery, including senior leadership of a recovery function handling high-value non-performing loans. Demonstrated experience across both high-ticket/corporate recovery (litigation-led, relationship-driven) and high-volume digital/retail collections (analytics-led, behavioral, tech-enabled)  Strong working knowledge of debt recovery laws, banking regulations, and court procedures in Nigeria. Familiarity with digital collections infrastructure and tactics — dialer/CRM systems, SMS/USSD/app-based nudges, propensity-to-pay scoring, and behavioral segmentation for low-ticket, high-volume portfolios. Demonstrated experience designing, building, or scaling a recovery/collections function — including org design, systems and process build-out, and team hiring. Proven experience overseeing recovery operations with national coverage, including a strong network of legal counsel and law enforcement contacts spanning all six geo-political zones in Nigeria — as opposed to experience confined to a single state or region. Excellent negotiation, problem-solving, and decision-making skills. Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret financial and portfolio data to guide recovery strategy. Relevant Skills Loan Recovery & Collections Strategy (high-ticket and digital/retail) Credit Risk Management Data Analytics, Propensity Scoring & Portfolio Reporting Digital Collections Tools & Automation Negotiation & Conflict Resolution People & Performance Management Organisational Design & Team Build-out What we can offer you Culture -We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human. Learning - We have a learning and development-focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing, training, and regular internal technical talks. Compensation - You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, annual bonus, plus other benefits. What to expect in the hiring process A preliminary phone call with the recruiter An interview with one of our credit business leads A behavioral and technical interview with a member of the Executive team.  Moniepoint is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

title: Head of Engineering, Field Verification
description: Who we are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Why South Africa   South Africa has one of the strongest engineering communities anywhere in the world, and we are deliberately growing our technology organisation in the country. We already have several team members based here. The work is fully remote, and the mission we are working on is a good deal closer to home than it is for our teams elsewhere. So, now we are looking for our Head of Engineering, Field Verification to join us in South Africa. About the role Field Verification is how Moniepoint knows that the people and businesses on our platform are real. Every Moniepoint customer, retail and business, requires a completed field verification as part of KYC. The platform coordinates physical, in-person checks — verifying individuals, business owners, business addresses and loan guarantors — and it serves nearly every part of the company: onboarding, loans, compliance and the fraud team. The system works today. A back office gives each business unit visibility and control over its own verification requests. A mobile-friendly web app puts the work in the hands of Field Verification Officers and the cluster leads who manage them across local government areas. An API layer lets other business units push verification requests in and receive results back by webhook, and an assignment algorithm routes each request to an officer close enough to carry it out. We want to be straightforward about the rest. This domain has never had a dedicated engineering leader, and that is the single biggest constraint on it. The team is one lean, cross-functional squad — an Engineering Manager, four engineers and a QA — carrying verification volume for the entire customer base. They have done that impressively well, but running lean means running in keep-the-lights-on mode, and a long list of things that would make this platform substantially better has been waiting for someone to own it. That list is the role. Trip and route management, so an officer can plan an optimal day across several sites rather than making a separate journey for each one — today we pay for a round trip per verification, and the logistics are nowhere near optimal. Capacity management. A native mobile app, wanted for a long time and never resourced. Liveness and identity verification tooling, exposed as APIs the rest of the business can build on. And as Moniepoint expands into markets where identity verification is as difficult as it is in Nigeria, Kenya among them, a platform that works beyond a single country. There is a great deal of room to build here. Whoever takes this on will set the direction rather than inherit someone else's plan, on a system that already carries real weight for the business. As Head of Engineering, Field Verification, your responsibilities will include: Owning the technical strategy, architecture and roadmap for the Field Verification platform end to end, and setting direction for a domain that has been running without dedicated engineering leadership. Moving the platform from keep-the-lights-on operation to deliberate, prioritised development. Leading and growing the existing cross-functional team, and building the organisation out as scope expands. Building the operational efficiency layer — trip and route optimisation, task allocation and capacity management for field officers. Owning the platform's client-facing surface: the APIs and webhooks that other business units integrate with, and the back office those units rely on. Delivering a native mobile experience for field officers. Ensuring verification data is structured, auditable and fit for compliance scrutiny. Building for multi-country expansion as Moniepoint enters new markets. Partnering closely with Product and with the business units that depend on the platform — onboarding, loans, compliance and fraud. Defining architecture standards, engineering processes and quality metrics, and hiring and developing engineers and Engineering Managers. Who you are You have built things yourself, and grew into leadership from there. We are explicit about this: we are not looking for someone who moved into management early and has led from a distance since. We want an engineer who became a leader. You are capable across disciplines. Backend, web and mobile. This platform spans all three and you will need credibility in each — a specialist in one layer will struggle here. You have built platforms, not just products. Systems used by several distinct groups of users and internal business units, with the flexibility to serve requirements you did not anticipate. You are a problem solver first. We would rather have someone adaptable than someone with the exact domain experience. Having built across different industries — fintech, e-commerce, logistics or otherwise — is a positive signal, not a scattered CV. You have 10+ years of overall software engineering experience, with substantial hands-on production engineering and strong backend depth. Our backend environment is Java and Spring Boot. You have at least 5 years of engineering leadership, including managing Engineering Managers. You collaborate well with product and business stakeholders, and can translate operational requirements into engineering solutions. Experience working with location and geospatial data is a strong plus, including map integrations. Experience with route, trip or delivery optimisation is a strong plus. Experience building for compliance — where data must be structured to evidence what was done and when — is a strong plus. Experience with identity, KYC or verification platforms is a plus. None of these four are requirements. Cultural Alignment As well, we assess every candidate across eight dimensions that define how great leaders operate at Moniepoint. We look for evidence of all eight throughout the process, not just in a single conversation. Customer Obsession: Build deep empathy for users. Solve problems intuitively, and fix root causes, not just tickets. Craft: Master the fundamentals. Reason from first principles, make trade-offs explicit, and raise the bar on quality. Systemisation: Turn repeating decisions into scalable mechanisms. Reduce cognitive load and raise engineering quality. Urgency: Move with disciplined speed. Act autonomously within scope, remove friction, and escalate risks early. Ownership: Treat the platform as your own. Take initiative across boundaries and follow through without reminders. No Ego: Put the mission first. Share credit, welcome debate, and never protect status over team outcomes. Candour: Surface uncomfortable truths and risks early. Intelligent failure is welcome; concealment is not. Integrity: Stay truthful and ethically consistent. Refuse toxic behavior. Performance without integrity is unacceptable. What Success Looks Like The domain has clear technical ownership and direction for the first time. The team out of keep-the-lights-on mode and delivering against a prioritised roadmap. Measurable improvement in field officer efficiency — more verifications per trip, lower cost per verification. A native mobile experience shipped for field officers. Verification data that stands up to compliance scrutiny across every business unit the platform serves. The platform ready to support a new market. A team grown beyond its current size, with a strong bench of engineers and managers. Why Join Us A genuinely greenfield mandate on a system that already matters. Every customer Moniepoint onboards passes through this platform. A lean, capable team making outsized impact, and the remit to build the organisation around them. Breadth: backend, web, mobile, location data, compliance and operational optimisation in one domain. Be part of a mission-driven company expanding access to financial services for millions of businesses and individuals. What To Expect in The Hiring Process A preliminary phone call with the recruiter. 60 minute High level System Design round with one of our Engineering Managers. 60 minute Panel Interview with 2 of our Head of Engineering leaders. 30 minutes focused on a technical deep dive into your CV and into a project or system you built in the past. 30 minutes focused on testing for leadership attributes. 60 minute Stakeholder Management Round with one of our Product Heads/VPs, focused on your stakeholder management and collaboration skills with product and business. 60 minute Technical round and Culture fit interview with our Co-founder & Group CTO (the hiring manager).

title: Head of Engineering, Rewards
description: Who we are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Why Poland Poland is a new and deliberate addition to our engineering map. We recently made our first technology hire in the country, and we see it as a long-term strategic location for senior hires, particularly within engineering. Joining now means joining early, and helping shape what our presence here becomes. So, now we are looking for our Head of Engineering, Rewards to join us in Poland. About The Role Rewards is one of the most strategically important platforms at Moniepoint, and it is being built into a dedicated charter with its own engineering and product leadership. The platform sits at the centre of our retention strategy across a user base of approximately 23 million people. Today the platform does one thing: cashback. It works, but it has barely scratched the surface of what rewards can be, and the cashback product itself is not yet built to the depth it deserves. The ambition is to evolve it into a full rewards, retention, engagement and personalisation platform — and to do that across the full 360 degrees of our network. That means rewards for our business customers, rewards for our consumer customers, and rewards for the sales agents who drive our distribution. Very few companies get to design this from close to a blank page at this scale. The Head of Engineering owns that platform end to end. You will inherit a team of nine engineers, including an Engineering Manager, and build the organisation out from there — the current expectation is a minimum of three product units and upwards of 25 people, though the eventual shape is genuinely yours to define. Your first objective is to get the best possible performance out of the cashback product we already have. From there, you will work with Growth, Sales and Marketing to determine what we build for acquisition and retention, and roll it out across every customer we serve. This is a consumer-facing product engineering role, and that is the most important thing to understand about it. Rewards is won or lost on experimentation, personalisation, and the quality of the experience in a customer's hands. We are looking for a leader who has built and shipped direct-to-consumer products at scale, who is fluent in experimentation and A/B testing, and who has real depth in front-end and mobile engineering — not a purely backend platform leader. Moniepoint runs a Domain CTO model. We view our Heads of Engineering as the CTO of their domain: you own the technical roadmap, the architecture, the delivery, and the organisation beneath you. You will have full autonomy over engineering strategy, architecture, hiring, operating cadence and roadmap trade-offs. You will report functionally to our Group CTO, with a dual reporting line into the Product leader for Rewards. That second line is a delivery relationship rather than a seniority one — engineering and product are peers here, and you will build the team to full capacity together. Your responsibilities as Head of Engineering, Rewards includes: Owning the technical strategy, architecture and roadmap for the Rewards Platform end to end. Improving the performance, reliability and depth of the existing cashback product as an immediate first priority. Evolving cashback into a broader rewards, retention, engagement and personalisation platform serving business customers, consumer customers and sales agents. Building the engineering organisation from its current base - structuring product units, hiring engineers and Engineering Managers, and leading through those managers as the team scales. Establishing a strong experimentation culture: A/B testing, cohort analysis, and measurement that lets the team learn quickly what actually changes customer behaviour. Working closely with Growth, Sales and Marketing to translate acquisition and retention objectives into product and engineering initiatives. Owning the customer-facing experience of rewards across mobile and web, including how quickly and reliably customers receive what they have earned. Define architecture standards, engineering processes and quality metrics, and own the engineering health of the domain — incidents, production defects, deployment frequency, change failure rate, and developer experience. Build the platform to serve customers across multiple geographies as Moniepoint expands. Partner with Product to define the rewards-specific metrics and OKRs that do not yet exist, and hold the team to them. Who You Are  Direct-to-consumer product engineering at scale. You have built and shipped products used directly by large consumer audiences, and you understand what moves engagement and retention. This is the defining requirement of the role. Genuine front-end and mobile depth. You have led or personally built consumer-facing mobile and web experiences. A backend-only background, however strong, is not what this role needs. Experimentation and growth engineering. Hands-on experience running A/B tests, feature flagging, and measurement frameworks, and using the results to drive product decisions rather than to justify them. At least 5 years of experience managing managers — leading an engineering organisation through other engineering leaders, not a single team. Hands-on technical leadership. You are still close to the code. We expect a meaningful proportion of hands-on engineering time and technical credibility with the engineers you lead. 10+ years of overall software engineering experience, with at least 5 years leading engineering teams through growth phases. title: Head, POS Recovery
description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Job Title: POS Recovery Manager Department: POS Channel Reports to: VP, POS Channel About this role: This role owns the end-to-end recovery of non-performing POS terminal assets — from the moment a terminal is flagged as at risk through to physical retrieval, financial settlement, and post-write-off recovery. Responsibilities Recovery Strategy Governance Own the terminal recovery lifecycle that defines escalation speed and settlement windows based on terminal age, transaction history, and recovery economics.  Ensure every terminal that enters recovery mode is assigned, tracked, escalated on schedule, and settled within its gate deadline — recovery, write-off, paid write-off, or insurance claim.  Design and continuously refine the recovery strategy, covering device collection, swap logistics, sales agent coordination, external agency management, and the efficient flow of assets back to custody.  Field Team Leadership Lead, manage, and hold accountable a distributed field recovery team across multiple regions.  Instill a culture of operational discipline, accountability, and ethical conduct. Recovery work involves sensitive situations (confronting custodians about lost assets, handling disputes, managing bounty payments); the team must operate with integrity.  Develop comprehensive standard operating procedures for every recovery scenario: BRM-led recovery, external agency coordination, business takeover, faulty terminal collection, voluntary write-off processing, dispute handling, revive processing.  Build training programmes for recovery agents covering: terminal identification, check-in procedures, evidence collection for disputes, GPS and field management tools, escalation protocols.  KPI Management and Recovery Economics Define and track recovery KPIs: recovery rate (pre-write-off), BRM recovery rate, external recovery rate, average days to recovery, cost per recovery, revive rate (post-write-off), bounty efficiency (bounty spend vs recovery value recovered).  Own the recovery economics: ensure total bounty spend plus logistics cost is always less than the recovery value of the terminals retrieved. The programme must be self-funding — recovery must generate more value than it costs.  Report monthly on: terminals entering recovery mode, terminals recovered, terminals written off, terminals revived, net financial impact, bounty spend, external agency spend, dispute volumes and outcomes.  Experience & Background Minimum 7 years of progressive experience managing large-scale field operations, logistics, asset recovery, or after-sales service, with at least 3 years in a senior leadership role.  Experience managing distributed field teams across multiple regions in Nigeria — you understand the infrastructure, the logistics constraints, and the human dynamics of field recovery operations.  Experience managing third-party service providers, contractors, or agency networks with performance-based contracts.  Direct experience in the Nigerian market with its specific logistical, regulatory, and operational realities.  Preferred: Experience from fintech, telecoms, e-commerce logistics, or any high-volume distributed asset management environment.  Preferred: Experience managing asset recovery at scale (thousands of units per month, not dozens).  Skills & Competencies Proven ability to design and implement structured operational processes (SOPs, escalation frameworks, settlement procedures) from scratch or through a major restructure.  Strong analytical capability — you use data to drive decisions, track performance, calculate ROI on recovery spend.  Financial discipline & budget management — experience managing a budget or cost centre, understanding unit economics, and demonstrating net positive recovery value.  Technical & Systems acumen — experience with product management/development lifecycles (writing briefs, working with engineers), GPS tracking, CRM, field management tools, or route optimisation platforms.  Regulatory & Compliance understanding — familiarity with insurance claim processes, write-off accounting, or asset disposal regulations in Nigeria.  What Success Looks Like in This Role Terminal recovery lifecycle is tightly governed, ensuring swift escalation and settlement within established gate deadlines.  Field recovery operations maintain high ethical standards and operational discipline across all regions.  Recovery program operates as a self-funding unit where total recovery value generated consistently exceeds total bounty and logistics expenditure.  Robust systems, SOPs, and field management tools are seamlessly integrated into daily team operations.  Transparent monthly reporting clearly demonstrates positive net financial impact and high recovery/revive rates.  Why Join Us?  Competitive compensation, benefits, and career growth opportunities.  Support for professional development and a dynamic culture driving financial inclusion across Africa.

title: Head, Product Control & Accounting
description: Who we are Moniepoint is Africa's all-in-one financial ecosystem, empowering businesses and their customers with seamless payment, banking, credit, and management tools. In 2023, we processed $182 billion and are Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer. Job Purpose Sits between Finance and the Product & Technology platform team, as products are built, ensuring every new product, feature, or pricing change is correctly designed from an accounting and control standpoint before it ships.Owns the thread from customer journey to financial reporting: how a product event is captured, how it maps to the chart of accounts, and how it lands in the Group's financial statements. Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out posts on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth. Responsibilities: Act as the standing technical accounting partner to Product and Engineering for all new products, features, and pricing changes Write technical accounting memos and position papers for new or changed products (revenue recognition under IFRS 15, financial instrument classification under IFRS 9, fee vs. interest income treatment, etc.) Design, build, and maintain the chart of accounts for new and existing products, ensuring consistency across entities Map each stage of the customer journey (onboarding, transaction, settlement, fee, reversal, write-off) to the correct GL treatment, end to end Review product and engineering specs pre-launch to flag accounting and control gaps before they reach production Own the reconciliation between product/transaction system data and the general ledger, and resolve breaks at source Design controls around new product flows (maker-checker, reconciliation, exception handling) and document them to audit standard Maintain a living library of accounting treatment documentation per product, kept current as products evolve Partner with Financial Control, Internal Audit, and external auditors on product-related technical accounting queries Candidate requirements: ACA / ACCA (or equivalent) with 8+ years post-qualification experience, including Big 4 technical accounting or audit background Strong working knowledge of IFRS 15 (revenue), IFRS 9 (financial instruments), and IFRS more broadly Experience translating a product or system design into accounting treatment and GL structure, not just reviewing after the fact Comfortable reading product specs and talking directly to engineers and product managers, not only to finance colleagues Preffered Qualifications Experience in payments, fintech, or banking, ideally with exposure to how transaction/ledger systems are built Prior experience designing or restructuring a chart of accounts for a multi-product platform Exposure to regulatory reporting requirements tied to product design (CBN, FCA, CBK or equivalent) Experience working inside or alongside an agile product/engineering team About You: You can sit in a product spec review and immediately see where the accounting will break, and say so before launch, not after You translate fluently between accountants and engineers without dumbing either side down You default to documenting the treatment properly rather than leaving it as tribal knowledge You're comfortable owning a chart of accounts as a living system, not a static reference document You care as much about the control design as the accounting answer. A technically correct treatment with no control around it isn't good enough What success looks like: No product ships without a documented, signed-off accounting treatment and GL mapping Chart of accounts stays clean and consistent as new products launch, with no post-hoc reclassification projects Product/transaction data reconciles to the GL within agreed tolerances, with breaks resolved at source, not papered over monthly Audit findings related to product accounting or control design trend toward zero Product and Engineering see Finance as a design partner, not a late-stage blocker What to expect in the hiring process A preliminary phone call with one of our recruiters. Hiring Manager Interview  A Panel interview with existing Finance Leads A behavioural and technical interview with a member of the Executive team.

title: Inventory Support Officer (South East)
description: Who We are Moniepoint Inc is a financial technology company digitizing Africa’s real economy by building a financial ecosystem for businesses, providing them with all the payment, banking, credit and business management tools they need to succeed.  What We do At Moniepoint, we are a customer-focused community, dedicated to crafting solutions that redefine our industry. We have several products that provide essential services for businesses such as credit, overdrafts etc. We leverage artificial intelligence and data to make our decisions but also have the technology and data-driven best practices used to support our businesses.  1A. Inventory Support Officer – POS Terminals Role Purpose The ISO (Terminals) is the dedicated custodian for all forms of POS terminals flowing through the repair pipeline. The role ensures end-to-end traceability, enforces custody controls, and maintains absolute logical–physical alignment within the Repair Centre's IMS subsystem, covering every stage from receipt of faulty units to dispatch of QA-cleared OK devices. Key Responsibilities Intake & Receipt Management Receive faulty/returned terminals from state offices; verify against the recall waybill at serial-number level before accepting into the IMS. Log all received devices in the IMS with correct status within 24 hours of physical arrival. Identify and quarantine damaged or missing-serial devices; raise a Discrepancy Report immediately. Repair Pipeline Tracking Push faulty devices to technicians daily and update IMS status to 'In Repair' upon assignment. Monitor movement of each terminal through all repair stages: Assessment → In Repair → Awaiting QA → QA Cleared → Dispatch Holding. Enforce the 24–72-hour SLA from receipt-to-assignment and from QA clearance-to-dispatch readiness. QA Integration & Status Management Receive QA-approved terminals and update IMS status to 'QA Cleared – Awaiting Dispatch' within 4 hours. Flag devices that fail QA back to the repair queue or classify as 'Beyond Economic Repair (BER)' with a written justification report. Ensure all 'BER' devices are tagged and isolated in the scrap/disposal holding area. Dispatch & Outbound Logistics Generate the Dispatch List and Waybill for QA-cleared refurbished and OK devices; obtain approval from Repair Centre Manager and Cluster lead before release. Scan all devices at serial level during physical loading; update IMS to 'In Transit – Outbound'. Confirm receipt acknowledgment from the destination state SIO and close the dispatch transaction in IMS. Inventory Counts & Reconciliation Conduct daily physical counts of all terminals in the repair centre; reconcile against IMS records. Escalate any variance (physical vs. logical) to the Lead, Inventory Support within the same business day. Participate in monthly, quarterly, and annual wall-to-wall counts as directed by the Inventory & Warehouse Manager. title: Lead, Channels and Audit Analytics
description: About us Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times, Moniepoint is Africa’s fastest-growing fintech, trusted by over 10 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of Naira in transactions monthly. Our mission is to enable financial happiness for every African, everywhere. Job Title: Lead, Channels and Audit Analytics  Department: Internal Audit  Reports to: Director, Product and Channels Audit  About this role The Lead, Channels & Audit Analytics will support the Chief Audit Officer and Director in strengthening assurance over Moniepoint's digital channels, payments ecosystem, products, and technology-enabled business processes through risk-based auditing and data-driven analytics. The role will lead the design and execution of channel audits, continuous auditing, and audit analytics initiatives to proactively identify emerging risks, assess the effectiveness of controls, and provide actionable insights that improve business performance, operational resilience, regulatory compliance, and customer experience. Responsibilities Audit Leadership & Execution: Lead risk-based audits across digital channels, payment products, customer journeys, and technology-enabled business processes, ensuring alignment with the Internal Audit Plan. Perform end-to-end audits covering product governance, digital channels, payment processing, customer onboarding, transaction lifecycle, operational resilience, cybersecurity controls, and technology change management. Audit Analytics & Continuous Monitoring: Design and execute audit analytics and continuous monitoring routines to identify control failures, emerging risks, fraud indicators, operational inefficiencies, and unusual transaction patterns. Develop data-driven audit procedures using SQL, Superset, Redash (Hera, Loki, Hela), Python, Power BI, Metabase, or similar analytical tools. Risk Assessment & Metric Tracking: Conduct enterprise risk assessments for digital channels, products, and payment ecosystems by evaluating inherent risks, control design, control effectiveness, and residual risks. Monitor Risk Performance Metrics across products and channels. Data Analysis & Insights: Analyse large and complex datasets to provide audit insights covering transaction integrity, customer behaviour, fraud trends, system performance, reconciliation, service availability, and regulatory compliance. Reporting & Quality Assurance: Review audit workpapers, evidence, and reports to ensure findings are supported by sufficient evidence and comply with Internal Audit standards. Prepare clear, concise, and impactful audit reports with practical recommendations that strengthen governance, risk management, and internal controls. Support continuous improvement of audit methodologies through automation, advanced analytics, AI-enabled auditing techniques, and dashboard reporting. Contribute to the achievement of Internal Audit strategic objectives, departmental KPIs, and quality assurance standards. Perform other duties assigned by the Chief Audit Officer and Director. Minimum of 7 years of progressive experience in Internal Audit, Audit Analytics, Data Analytics, Technology Audit, Risk Management, or Consulting within the financial services or fintech industry. At least one (1) of the following professional certifications: ACA, ACCA, CPA, CIA, CISA, or CFE. A Master's degree or professional certification in Data Analytics, Business Intelligence, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, or a related analytical discipline will be an added advantage. Proven experience developing audit analytics, continuous auditing routines, and dashboard reporting that enhance audit effectiveness and business decision-making. We need someone who thinks in systems, works from first principles, and has the depth to make credible judgements on strategy, technology, and economics simultaneously. acquisition Build and maintain campaign structures optimised for Moniepoint's dual-product funnel — separating signals, audiences, and bidding logic appropriately across segments Set bidding strategies, budget allocation frameworks, and creative testing cycles that reduce dependence on any single signal or format Own campaign performance end-to-end: from brief to launch to optimisation to reporting Tracking, Attribution & Technical Infrastructure Architect and own the full measurement stack: Firebase / GA4 event taxonomy, Google Tag Manager configuration, and server-side event pipelines Lead the implementation and ongoing integrity of Conversion APIs and enhanced conversions to maximise signal quality sent back to Google Define the attribution model — evaluate last-click, data-driven, and custom models against Moniepoint's funnel reality, and own the decision with clear reasoning Partner with engineering and data teams to ensure event data flowing to Google is accurate, complete, and timely — treating signal quality as a competitive asset Build audit protocols for tracking coverage and attribution consistency; surface gaps before they distort decisions LTV/CAC Economics Own the economic model for Google acquisition: define CAC targets by product, segment, and channel variant; set the inputs, assumptions, and review cadence Understand the LTV/CAC relationship at a structural level — not just as a ratio to optimise, but as a function of product retention, monetisation curves, and cohort behaviour Build and iterate on payback period models that account for Moniepoint's emerging market context: irregular income patterns, higher churn risk, and longer monetisation timelines Design bidding and budget logic that reflects true LTV signals rather than proxy metrics, working closely with data science to enrich Google's Smart Bidding with offline conversion data Proactively identify when CAC is drifting against LTV thresholds and lead the diagnosis — channel mix, audience quality, creative fatigue, product-market fit — before it becomes a financial problem Governance & Reporting Build a channel reporting system that surfaces reality clearly — not dashboards that flatter performance, but views that drive better decisions Establish review cadences with clear owners, metrics, and follow-through mechanisms Translate channel performance into business language for senior stakeholders: what is the cost of growth, is it sustainable, and what would change the trajectory Emerging Market & Fintech Context Adapt Google acquisition strategy for the realities of emerging market users: variable device penetration, low-bandwidth environments, trust barriers to financial services, and diverse language/literacy contexts Navigate platform constraints specific to fintech advertising on Google: financial services policies, verification requirements, and creative compliance Bring genuine insight into what acquisition patterns distinguish sustainable fintech growth from subsidised growth in markets like Nigeria To succeed in this role, you should have: 6+ years of hands-on paid acquisition experience, with the majority of that time spent on Google UAC / App Campaigns at meaningful scale Deep, demonstrable technical knowledge of Google's campaign infrastructure: bidding algorithms, audience signals, creative specs, and the mechanics of Smart Bidding Proven ability to architect and own the full measurement stack — Firebase, GA4, GTM, Conversion APIs — not just configure it but understand why each component matters Fluency in LTV/CAC modelling: you have built the models, owned the assumptions, and used them to make real budgeting and bidding decisions Experience operating in a fintech or financial services context, with direct knowledge of the acquisition compliance and trust dynamics unique to financial products Strongly Preferred Experience running Google acquisition in Sub-Saharan Africa or comparable emerging markets — Nigeria specifically is a significant advantage Familiarity with server-side conversion APIs, offline conversion imports, and enhanced conversions as mechanisms for improving signal quality in cookieless or app-first environments Experience working with data science or analytics teams to build custom bidding signals and offline LTV imports into Google's systems Prior work on dual-product or dual-segment acquisition (e.g., consumer and SME / business) with separate funnel logic What Success Looks Like In the first 90 days Full audit of existing Google campaign structure, tracking integrity, and attribution model completed — with a written assessment and prioritised improvement plan Measurement stack gaps identified and remediation underway with engineering LTV/CAC baseline model built with documented assumptions, reviewed with Growth and Finance First governance cadence established — weekly performance review with clear owner, metrics, and follow-through log In the first year Google channel operating as a reliable, scalable growth engine with predictable CAC across both personal and business banking segments Signal quality measurably improved — higher match rates, cleaner conversion data, reduced reliance on last-click proxies Attribution model validated against actual cohort data and actively used in budget allocation decisions Playbook documented: campaign architecture, bidding logic, audience strategy, and economic model all institutionalised — not living in one person's head A team (or foundations for one) built with title: Product Auditor
description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. What We Do At Moniepoint, we are a customer-focused community dedicated to crafting solutions that redefine our industry. We leverage artificial intelligence and data-driven best practices to support our businesses, from providing credit and overdrafts to ensuring every transaction is secure. Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out our stories on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth. Role Overview The Product Auditor provides independent assurance over the design, implementation, and operating effectiveness of product controls across payment, wallet, settlement, switches and other related products across the organisation The role ensures that new and existing products are deployed with adequate financial, operational, security, and regulatory controls, safeguarding the organization against revenue leakage, settlement failures, regulatory breaches, and technology-driven risks. The Product Auditor will independently evaluate product risk exposure and control maturity prior to scale. Key Responsibilities  Audit Universe & Risk-Based Planning Maintain a living Product Audit Universe covering all payment products, features, and integrations ranked by risk.  Own the annual Product Audit Plan, ensuring coverage is allocated dynamically based on risk ratings, product complexity, regulatory sensitivity, and change velocity. Product Design & Control Assurance Review PRDs, business rules, and transaction workflows to identify logic gaps, unmitigated risk paths, and missing exception-handling routines before products reach production/go-live.  Analyse product path scenarios, verify Maker-Checker enforcement, and provide formal control design sign-off before any material release goes live. Live Product Assessment ( Continuous Audit Review) Periodically assess live payment products to confirm they continue to operate within approved design parameters.  Detect configuration drift, identify silent divergence from original PRDs, and analyse live transaction data for emerging risk patterns. Go-Live Readiness & Control Gate Execute mandatory pre-production Product Audit reviews as an independent control gate for all material releases.  Confirm reconciliation logic, exception queues, and fallback controls are tested and functional.  Escalate critical deficiencies with risk ratings and hold recommendations where a product is not safe to release. Transaction Logic & Mathematical Integrity Interrogate the Fee Engine using SQL to mathematically prove that commissions, VAT, discounts, and splits are posted with complete precision.  Validate duplicate prevention mechanisms and ensure transaction integrity within complex, multi-step payment sequences, and test reversal, refund, and chargeback logic to confirm financial symmetry is maintained in every scenario. Settlement & Ledger Integrity Trace fund flows, confirming continuous synchronisation between wallet sub-ledgers and the General Ledger.  Assess reconciliation logic for breaks and evaluate the authorisation, documentation, and reversibility of manual settlement overrides. Product Change & Configuration Integrity Confirm that all product modifications: fee tables, routing rules, limit parameters passed through an approved change management cycle.  Identify silent changes made outside formal release processes and audit the integrity of product master data to ensure it is access-controlled, version-tracked, and consistent with approved product terms. Vendor & Third-Party Product Risk Assess controls over vendor-managed product components, evaluate SLA performance against contractual commitments, and identify single-vendor dependency risks within critical payment flows.  Evaluate the organisation's ability to detect unilateral changes in third-party API behaviour, fee logic, or settlement processes. Control Advisory & Stakeholder Engagement Engage product and engineering teams early in the design cycle to provide informal control advisory, reducing findings at the formal review stage without compromising independence.  Participate in design reviews and architecture discussions, and build a control-by-design culture across product teams.  Incident Review, RCA & Regulatory Alignment Lead post-incident reviews for product failures,producing structured RCA reports that identify underlying logic failures, not just surface symptoms.  Assess corrective actions for adequacy and track findings to verify closure.  Ensure product logic complies with CBN guidelines, PCI DSS, and consumer protection obligations at the design level, and evaluate the regulatory impact of new features before release. Reporting & Governance Prepare risk-rated audit reports for Executive Management and the Audit Committee, leading with findings, financial impact, and required action.  Maintain a Product Risk Register, deliver quarterly control maturity updates, and ensure governance bodies are never surprised by a product failure that was visible at the design or portfolio review stage. Required Knowledge & Skills  Technical Skills Advanced SQL for independent data extraction and transaction interrogation Payment systems architecture : Wallets, card processing, direct debit, settlement, and reconciliation API and integration literacy (Basic) End-to-end transaction lifecycle knowledge: Authorisation, posting, clearing, settlement, and exception handling PRD and process flow analysis: translating product documentation into control flowcharts Mathematical precision: fee calculations, interest computations, and split payment structures Pattern recognition: detecting anomalies, outliers, and irregularities in large transaction datasets Audit & Risk Skills Risk-based audit methodology: IIA Standards and COSO framework applied to financial products. Control design logic and evaluation Root cause analysis Regulatory knowledge: CBN payment system regulations, PCI DSS, NDPR,Nigerian consumer protection obligations etc Interpersonal & Professional Skills Stakeholder engagement Professional scepticism and independence Risk-rated report writing Tools & Platforms SQL (PostgreSQL / MySQL / MSSQL) AdvancedExcel / Google Sheets Claude / AI Tools Qualifications Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Finance, or a related quantitative discipline Experience: 3–5+ years in Product Audit, Systems Audit, Financial Data Analytics, or Payment Operations within a fintech or financial services environment Certifications: CISA, CIA, or CFE preferred. ACA / ACCA is acceptable when combined with strong technical product experience and data analytics. Sector Knowledge: Demonstrated hands-on familiarity with payment product architecture, wallet systems, and regulated payment flows in a Nigerian or comparable market context. What We Offer You Culture: We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’re human, we listen, and we look out for one another. Learning: We’re big on growth. You’ll find an environment focused on knowledge sharing, training, and helping you reach your potential. Compensation: You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, and an annual bonus, along with other great benefits. What to Expect in the Hiring Process A preliminary phone call with our recruiter. An interview with the hiring team. A final conversation with a member of our executive team. Moniepoint Inc. is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

title: Product Design Manager - Design System
description: Who we are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial ecosystem, helping 10 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, and business management tools since 2019. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, it powers most of the country’s Point of Sale (POS) transactions. Through its subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes $22 billion monthly for its customers while operating profitably. Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out posts on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth. About This Role We are looking for a Product Design Manager - Design System who thinks at a system level and understands how to create a scalable UI ecosystem that spans multiple products, teams, and platforms. You are not just designing static screens; you are building the foundation of our product user interfaces. In this role, you will take full ownership of our component libraries, interaction models, and cross-platform design consistency. You will act as the bridge between design and engineering, ensuring that our visual assets translate seamlessly into clean, reusable, and accessible production code.  Responsibilities UI Craft & Visual Excellence: Maintain an exceptionally high standard for layout, typography, colour, spacing, visual hierarchy, and overall digital finish across all reusable elements. Component Architecture: Design, build, and maintain robust component libraries (buttons, inputs, cards, navigation, forms, tables, etc.) that scale seamlessly across products. Interaction & Motion Design: Define interactive behaviors and state transitions (e.g., hover, focus, disabled, loading, and mobile behaviors) to ensure components feel alive and intuitive. Design Token Management: Structure and maintain design tokens (colours, spacing, typography, border-radius, shadows) to drive consistency between design environments and code. Figma Library Architecture: Organize complex variants, properties, and components within Figma to empower other product designers to build quickly and accurately. Engineering Collaboration: Partner closely with engineering teams to navigate technical constraints across Web, React, Flutter, Android, and iOS/Native app environments. Documentation & Governance: Create clear, comprehensive usage guidelines and documentation outlining when, why, and how components should (and should not) be used. Experience & Background Proven Design System Track Record: Extensive experience building, scaling, and maintaining production-ready design systems rather than just standalone product features. Cross-Platform Expertise: Deep understanding of the constraints and guidelines governing multiple platforms, including Web, iOS, and Android. Systems-Thinking Mindset: A portfolio demonstrating how individual design decisions impact multiple products, scale sustainably, and optimize designer/engineer workflows. Front-End Alignment: Strong familiarity with how developers inspect, build, and consume components in code repositories. Skills & Competencies Expert Figma Proficiency: Advanced knowledge of Figma libraries, auto-layout, components, variants, variables, and library publication. Accessibility Champion: Solid grasp of accessibility standards (WCAG), contrast requirements, and inclusive design principles. Technical Literacy: Familiarity with component-driven frameworks (React, Flutter) and Atomic Design methodology. Communication & Documentation: Excellent writing and presentation skills, with an ability to translate complex design system choices into clear executive-level updates and technical guidelines.  What Success Looks Like in This Role High Adoption & Efficiency: Design and engineering teams actively use the system, resulting in significantly accelerated product shipping cycles. Flawless Cross-Platform Consistency: A unified look, feel, and interactive behavior across all customer-facing touchpoints (Web, Android, iOS). Best-in-Class Documentation: A central, living source of truth that leaves no ambiguity regarding design tokens, component rules, or brand compliance. Scalable Architecture: A foundational library that handles future product expansions, rebrands, or theme changes with minimal friction.  Why Join Us Competitive compensation, benefits, and career growth opportunities. Fully remote work culture and support for professional development. What to expect in the hiring process Application & portfolio review: we assess your experience, leadership impact, and Design System case studies that demonstrate strategic thinking, process, and measurable outcomes. Preliminary phone call with recruiter: a brief conversation to discuss your background, leadership experience, and expectations. Interview with senior leadership: a deep dive into your leadership approach, design philosophy, and ability to drive impact. This includes a discussion on past projects and collaboration with cross-functional teams. Design leadership challenge: a scenario-based assessment to assess both strategic thinking and leadership skills while balancing UX/UI expertise. Final executive conversation: a discussion with senior leadership to assess alignment with our vision, strategic thinking, and team-building philosophy. How to apply: Submit your resume and portfolio showcasing your leadership in managing design teams, driving strategy, and delivering user-centred solutions with measurable business impact. We want to see case studies that demonstrate how you have led and developed designers, prioritised and managed projects, and fostered a high-performing team culture. Your portfolio should highlight how you have used research, data, and experimentation to inform decisions, optimise workflows, and drive success metrics.

title: Regional Marketing Specialist, NE
description: Who we are  Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. About the role The Regional Marketing Specialist is a strategic bridge between central brand directives and local market execution. You will be responsible for driving brand dominance and customer acquisition within your assigned region. By leveraging localized insights, you will ensure Moniepoint is the first choice for consumers and that our physical and digital presence translates into measurable growth in market share and accounts opened. What you will do Strategic Planning & Budgeting Campaign Planning: Develop quarterly regional marketing calendars aligned with the bank’s national strategy but tailored to local cultural/economic nuances. Financial Oversight: Manage the regional marketing budget; perform monthly reconciliations and ensure all vendors are onboarded and paid per procurement policy. ROI Analysis: Track the "Cost Per Acquisition" (CPA) for all regional activities to ensure high-impact spending. Local Brand & Identity Management Branding Implementation: Act as the "Brand Guardian" for the region, ensuring all branches, ATMs, and signage meet corporate visual identity standards. Local Media Buying: Identify and manage high-impact local visibility opportunities (e.g., regional radio, billboards in high-traffic markets, or community sponsorships). Competitor Intelligence: Monitor local competitor moves and provide monthly reports on their pricing, visibility, and tactics. Sales Support & Market Activations Neighborhood Activations: Design and execute high-energy "storming" exercises in key markets, transport hubs, and residential clusters to generate immediate leads. Sales Enablement: Provide the regional sales team with the necessary collateral (flyers, branded merchandise, and digital assets) to close leads effectively. Community & Relationship Marketing (Added Duties) Stakeholder Engagement: Build relationships with local traditional rulers, trade unions, and community leaders to facilitate "entry" into new market segments. Customer Feedback Loop: Conduct informal focus groups or surveys during activations to gather insights on local pain points and product gaps. CSR Coordination: Identify local charitable or community causes that align with the bank’s values to boost regional goodwill. Who you are  Education & Experience Education: Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business Administration, or a related field. Experience: 4–6 years of progressive marketing experience, ideally within the Financial Services, FMCG, or Telecommunications sectors. Key Skills & Competencies Data Analysis: Proficient in analyzing market data and performance metrics to derive actionable insights and inform decision-making. Event & Project Management: Proven track record in planning, coordinating, and executing large-scale events and marketing activations end-to-end. title: Senior Principal, Talent Marketing
description: About us Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times as Africa's fastest-growing fintech, Moniepoint is trusted by over 10 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of dollars in transactions monthly. Having built resilient, high-volume financial infrastructure that powers commerce across emerging markets, Moniepoint is embarking on its next phase of global scale. About this role As our Senior Principal, Talent Marketing, you will be the strategic architect responsible for establishing Moniepoint's talent brand and candidate pipeline in new markets from scratch. Where Moniepoint is not yet an established consumer brand, you will solve complex talent acquisition problems by understanding how senior engineers, engineering managers, and technical leaders think, connect, and evaluate career moves across Europe. Working from a blank piece of paper with high autonomy, you will translate our global Employer Value Proposition (EVP) into localized, high-converting talent marketing strategies. You will bridge the gap between Talent Acquisition, Engineering Leadership, and Brand - combining developer community immersion, high-touch physical events, and targeted campaigns that turn brand discovery into qualified, closed engineering hires.   Responsibilities 1. Zero-to-One Market Entry & Tech Hub Architecture Define European Hub Talent Strategy: Architect and lead the talent go-to-market strategy for Moniepoint's newest engineering hubs (principally Poland and Spain), crafting localized narratives that appeal to discerning software engineers. Anchor the 'Founding Team' Narrative: Position early European engineering cohorts as foundational builders, creating compelling narratives around technical scale, system complexity, and ownership that resonate with elite technical talent. Navigate Market Nuances: Diagnose and navigate country-specific developer dynamics—recognizing that developer communities in Poland, Spain, and the UK behave differently and require tailored engagement models rather than copy-pasted playbooks. 2. Developer Community, Ecosystem & Event Activation High-Impact Physical & Virtual Presence: Conceive, curate, and lead our physical presence at key developer conferences, engineering meetups, hackathons, and university partnerships across target markets. End-to-End Pipeline Activation: Ensure events are never vanity exercises; architect end-to-end follow-up systems and talent nurture funnels that convert event attendees into active, screened pipelines for our TA partners. Developer Platform Immersion: Leverage deep knowledge of where engineers consume information (e.g., GitLab/GitHub communities, tech forums, Discord/Slack groups, Meetup, Eventbrite) to drive authentic engagement. 3. Strategic Hiring Campaigns & Technical Enablement Targeted Campaign Architecture: Partner with TA leads and Engineering Directors to identify acute hiring bottlenecks and build agile, multi-channel marketing campaigns that address specialized, hard-to-fill tech disciplines. Technical EVP Translation: Translate technical architecture, distributed systems challenges, and fintech infrastructure realities into authentic, intellectually rigorous technical messaging that outshines local competitors. Recruiter Enablement & Narrative Toolkits: Equip our technical sourcing and recruitment teams with high-leverage narrative assets—outbound pitch decks, technical one-pagers, culture collateral, and messaging sequences that double recruiter outreach conversion. 4. Performance, Analytics & Optimization Hiring-Centric Metrics: Discard vanity metrics. Evaluate every initiative against pipeline contribution, qualified applicant rates, candidate quality score, cost-per-hire, and time-to-fill. Budget Oversight: Own and allocate dedicated talent marketing budgets with extreme commercial discipline—scaling programs that drive measurable hires and rapidly decommissioning initiatives that underdeliver. Paid Acquisition (Tactical Lever): Oversee and strategically deploy paid recruitment marketing spend across relevant technical platforms and channels when targeted outbound and community channels require acceleration. 5. Strategic Leadership & Scalability Strategic Thought Partnership: Serve as the trusted advisor to the Head of Talent Acquisition, VP of Engineering, and Brand Leadership on talent market intelligence, competitor positioning, and developer sentiment. Playbook Documentation: Establish and document Moniepoint's global talent expansion playbook, creating scalable frameworks that will be deployed across future international markets. Mentorship & Functional Growth: Provide strategic guidance to broader TA and brand team members, with the opportunity to mentor or direct junior talent marketing specialists as the function scales. Experience & Background 8+ Years of Talent Marketing Leadership: Experience leading talent marketing, technical recruitment marketing, or developer relations/advocacy, with substantial time dedicated to hiring software engineering and product disciplines. European Market Expertise: Demonstrated experience building talent brand presence and hiring pipelines across European tech ecosystems (particularly Central/Eastern Europe such as Poland, and Western/Southern Europe such as the UK or Spain). Zero-to-One Market Entry Track Record: Proven success entering new geographies or scaling talent brand where the employer brand was nascent or non-existent, creating playbooks from a blank sheet of paper. Fintech & Scale Exposure: Experience in hyper-growth fintech, high-frequency/payments infrastructure, or high-scale distributed systems environments. International Collaboration: Experience collaborating with international founding teams or distributed tech hubs across emerging and mature markets. Skills & Competencies Mastery in Event-Driven Pipeline Activation: Extensive hands-on experience designing and executing physical and digital developer events and architecting the subsequent candidate nurturing journey that yields hires. Deep Engineering Domain Fluency: Genuine understanding of software engineering culture, tech stacks (distributed systems, backend, infra, DevOps), and developer channels (Meetup, Eventbrite, GitLab/GitHub, Reddit, tech conferences). Comfort with Substantial Ambiguity: High agency and entrepreneurial drive; ability to make decisive bets, test hypotheses, and build structure in fast-moving, high-growth environments. Strategic Campaign Design: Ability to connect high-level EVP strategy to pragmatic, sprint-based talent acquisition sprints that deliver on an aggressive hiring plan (500+ tech hires). Paid Digital Campaign Optimization: Direct experience running and optimizing paid digital recruitment advertising campaigns independently across social and developer networks. What success looks like in this role First 30 Days (Discovery & Immersion): Map the competitive landscape and developer talent dynamics in Poland and Spain. Establish alignment with technical hiring leads (PEP, Engineering Directors) and TA leads to define immediate priority pipelines. Audit existing employer brand collateral and identify localized messaging gaps for European tech hiring. First 90 Days (Initial Market Entry & Quick Wins): Launch the first pilot physical event / developer meetup presence in Poland with a complete post-event pipeline conversion funnel. Roll out the European Recruiter Enablement Toolkit (localized pitch decks, outreach sequences, and technical one-pagers). Launch targeted marketing sprints for top 3 hardest-to-fill senior technical roles. First 6 Months (Hub Establishment & Pipeline Ramp): Position Moniepoint as a recognized, compelling engineering hub in Poland, supporting the identity and pride of the founding engineer cohort. Consistently contribute qualified, pre-warmed candidate pipelines directly supporting the ramp toward 500 tech/product hires. Prove multi-channel attribution showing which community and marketing initiatives are yielding quality hires. Year One (Global Expansion Playbook): Complete Moniepoint's International Talent Expansion Playbook, ready to be deployed across future tech hubs. Measurably decrease time-to-fill and increase direct outbound response rates across all European technical roles. Solidify Moniepoint's reputation as an employer of choice for Europe's most ambitious engineers. Why join us High-Impact Mission: Play a career-defining role in building the engineering backbone of Africa's fastest-growing fintech as it scales globally. True Ownership & Dedicated Resources: Autonomy to build from scratch with dedicated budget backing and direct executive sponsorship. Front-Row Seat to Tech Hub Creation: Help build engineering hubs from their inception, shaping culture, talent standards, and brand identity. Competitive Executive Package: Competitive base salary (calibrated for Senior Principal level), performance bonuses, comprehensive private healthcare, and pension schemes. Moniepoint is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

Job Summary We are seeking an experienced SRE to engineer the reliability of our highly distributed platform. You will combine deep knowledge of distributed systems with strong coding skills to define SLOs, lead incident response, and build automation and self-healing mechanisms into our systems. You will balance immediate operational stability with long-term strategic engineering to ensure our services scale linearly with our hyper-growth. Responsibilities Participate in on-call rotations as the primary technical lead. Act as the Incident Commander during major severity incidents: initiating war rooms, coordinating cross-functional teams, and providing clear status updates. Instrument code to expose high-cardinality metrics and distributed traces. Collaboratively define, measure, and defend Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and Error Budgets with product owners. Write high-quality, production-ready code (in Java, Go, or Python) to build internal tooling, automation platforms, and self-healing mechanisms that eliminate manual operator intervention. Partner with Product Engineering teams during the design phase to ensure new services are built with reliability, scalability, and observability patterns (circuit breakers, rate limiting, backpressure, fallback strategies) from day one. Analyze system performance and traffic patterns to model future capacity needs. Conduct load testing and chaos engineering experiments to verify system resilience under failure conditions.. Requirements Minimum of 5 years of experience in SRE or Backend Engineering with a strong ability to write clean, performant, and tested code in Java, Go, Rust, or Python. Deep understanding of distributed systems architecture and design patterns. You possess a strong command of microservices fundamentals, event-driven architectures, and the underlying principles required to build systems that scale. Extensive experience with Google Cloud Platform (GCP) or similar cloud providers (AWS/Azure). You are proficient in running production workloads on Kubernetes (GKE/EKS) and troubleshooting cluster/infrastructure issues.
